implementation_notes: Kotlin uses the Java persistence stack, so the joined strategy is declared, not coded: annotate the root with @Entity @Inheritance(strategy = InheritanceType.JOINED) and a @DiscriminatorColumn and the provider joins the per-class tables, with each subclass storing only the columns it declares. Kotlin-specific machinery replaces the classic boilerplate: entities must be open, which the all-open / kotlin-spring compiler plugin arranges for annotated classes, and they need a no-arg constructor path (Kotlin defaults or the kotlin-jpa plugin) because the persistence provider instantiates them reflectively. Data classes are the wrong tool for entities and Kotlin-native query libraries such as Exposed leave you writing the join by hand.
pitfalls: Kotlin classes are final by default; an entity compiled without all-open/kotlin-spring cannot be subclassed by the provider, so lazy loading and proxies fail at runtime.

Non-null properties without defaults break reflective no-arg construction, and data classes generate equals/copy semantics the persistence context does not expect - neither belongs in an entity hierarchy.
